title: The vocabulary
lede: 52 legal ideas, each drawn from the section 43 material and each signed off by a named reviewer. Held as {{SKOS}} — a standard for controlled vocabularies: a preferred label, the variants that mean the same thing, and the ones that do not.

items.label: Standing outside any hierarchy
items.note: a flat list is a list with extra steps

items.label: Sorted into a kind
items.note: ground of refusal / test / factor / exception

blocks.title: The biggest single gap, and it needs one pass by one person
blocks.text: All 52 ideas sit in the model as a bare *legal concept*. Whether *connotation* is a **test** the decision maker applies or a **factor** feeding into one is a legal judgement, so the four slots for it are declared and empty. Filling them is one pass over a list for someone who knows the domain, and it is what turns a flat vocabulary into something later stages can generalise over.
